his farm near Lewes, Tuesday,
December 49, Minos Conoway, Sc,
was stricken with a fatal heart
attack. He and some neighboring
farmers were doing their fall
butchering on the farm Conoway
had operated the past 80 years.
He was taken to the Beebe Hos
pital in the Lewes Fire Company
ambulance where he was pronoun-
ced dead on arrival


A native of Georgetown, son of
the late Minos T. and Virgil P.
Conoway, survivors are his widow,
Mrs. Anna M. Conoway, Nassau:
two daughters, Mrs. Charles
Moore of Georgetown, and Mrs.
Joseph Thoroughgood of Reho-
both Beach,; three sons, Melloy of
Nassau, Elberson of Waterford,
New York, Clifton of rural Lewes.
Another son, Minos T. Conoway,
was killed in France during World
War II, while serving with the
Seventh Infantry, U. S. Army.


He also leaves two brothers,
Fred of Georgetown, and John of
Millsboro; sister, Mrs. Edgar
Shockley of Oxon, Maryland: ten
grandchildren, and one great
grandchild


Funeral services will be held to-
day (Friday) at p. m. at the
Funeral Home, Lewes, with
the Rev Kenneth Dickey, pastor
of Whites Chapel, officiating.
Burial will be in the chapel
churchyard.
